text.p: The Anaheim Angels released one future Hall of Famer to make room for another Thursday when they released eight-time All-Star Eddie Murray to make room for newly acquired Rickey Henderson.

Murray, 41, is hitting just .219 (35-for-160) with three homers and 15 RBI in 46 games for the Angels this season. He became expendable when Henderson was acquired from the San Diego Padres on Wednesday for two minor-leaguers and a player to be named.

Murray has played for the Baltimore Orioles (1977-88, 1996), Los Angeles Dodgers (1989-91), New York Mets (1992-93), Cleveland Indians (1994-96) and Angeles in his 21-year career. A lifetime .287 hitter, Murray has 3,253 hits, including 504 homers, and 1,914 RBI in 3,017 games.

He is sixth on the all-time games list, seventh in RBI, ninth in hits and 15th in homers. In addition, he is second with 19 grand slams, fifth with 11,329 at-bats, seventh with 5,395 total bases and 13th with 560 doubles. Murray, Hank Aaron and Willie Mays are the only players with more than 3,000 hits and 500 homers.
Murray won a World Series with the 1983 Baltimore Orioles and was on the losing side for Baltimore in 1979 and the Indians in 1995.
